Lemma
[a tangent geodesic with positive Hessian stays outside]

1. ch3:4.1If $F:\mathbb {R}\to \mathbb {R}$ is continuous at $0$ with $F'(0)=0$ and $F''(0)>0$, then $F(t)\ge F(0)$ for all $t$ near $0$. With $F=|u|_p^2$ and $F(0)=r^2$, a geodesic tangent to $S_r(p)$ at $\gamma (0)$ keeps $|\exp _p^{-1}\gamma (t)|^2\ge r^2$, i.e. does not re-enter the open ball $B_r(p)$.
Proof

\sketch

The second-derivative test: $F'(0)=0$ and $F''(0)>0$ give a local minimum of $F$ at $0$, so $F(t)\ge F(0)$ near $0$.

□
